title: Paddy + Fish Integrated Farming
subtitle: Successful models from India and China, and a practical implementation roadmap for paddy-growing districts of Andhra Pradesh
audience: Case study deck for district & mandal officials
source_note: Focus: dual productivity, farmer income, nutrition, sustainability and mandal-level execution. Visual generated for training use; data sources on relevant slides.

sections.title: Why paddy + fish integration matters for Andhra Pradesh
sections.source: Sources: AP Seeds paddy crop note; CGIAR, 2023; TNAU fishery integration note.

items.desc: West Godavari, East Godavari and Krishna are among the most important rice-producing districts of Andhra Pradesh and India.
Rice monoculture often faces cost, price and climate risks. Fish adds a second output from the same field and water.
Coastal and delta districts already have farmers, markets and departments familiar with fish seed, stocking and marketing.

blocks.title: Policy fit for AP
items: Supports district GVA growth through allied-sector income.
Works well with natural farming, water-efficiency and nutrition goals.
Creates a field-level demonstration model that officers can scale through RBKs and mandal teams.

sections.title: The model: one paddy field, two harvests
sections.source: Sources: FAO GIAHS Qingtian Rice-Fish Culture; UNDP/NITI Assam rice-fish case.

items.desc: Fish manure fertilizes soil; fish movement aerates water and softens soil; fish eat larvae, weeds and insects.
Rice canopy provides shade; the flooded field gives habitat; plankton and organic matter support fish growth.
Raised bunds, fish refuge trench/pond, screened inlet/outlet, controlled water depth and safe harvest channel.
Rice calendar must align with stocking; pesticide use must be avoided or carefully controlled.

blocks.label: Core lesson
blocks.text: this is not "fish added to paddy"; it is a planned field system requiring water control, species choice and farmer training.

sections.title: India case study 1: Climate-resilient rice–fish farming in Assam
sections.source: Source: UNDP SDG Knowledge Hub / NITI for States, "Climate Resilient Rice–Fish Farming in Assam".

blocks.text: Implemented by the Fishery Department, Assam during 2018–19 to 2020–21 as a climate-resilient livelihood model.

blocks.title: Reported outcomes
items: Average rice production reported around 7 tonnes/ha/year.
Reduced weeding labour and improved local fish availability.

blocks.label: Learning for AP officials
blocks.text: Start with technically suitable fields and invest in handholding. The model succeeds when fisheries and agriculture staff work together through a common mandal plan.

sections.title: India case study 2: Apatani paddy-cum-fish farming, Arunachal Pradesh
sections.source: Source: Directorate of Fisheries, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, "Paddy-cum-fish-culture".

blocks.title: Why this model is important
items: Widely practiced in the Apatani plateau and described by the state fisheries department as profitable and sustainable.
Generates two crops — paddy and fish — from the same cultivable area.
Uses low-lying fields, raised bunds, irrigation channels and suitable carp species.

items.label: recommended bund height in government note

blocks.label: Transferable lesson
blocks.text: Rice–fish integration works best when water channels, community rules and farmer skills are designed together — not as isolated input distribution.

sections.title: China case study: Qingtian Rice–Fish Culture System
sections.source: Sources: FAO GIAHS Qingtian Rice-Fish Culture; Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems, 2024.

blocks.title: What makes it successful
items: Fish fertilize rice, disturb water, soften soil, and eat larvae and weeds.
Rice gives fish shade, food and habitat.
Lower-cost inputs reduce use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides and herbicides.
Heritage branding supports higher-value products and rural revitalization.

blocks.label: Learning for AP
blocks.text: protect ecology + build product identity. This can become a "safe rice + local fish" brand, not just a production technique.

sections.title: What the India and China cases have in common
sections.source: Sources synthesized from Assam case, Arunachal Pradesh fisheries note and FAO Qingtian GIAHS documentation.

items.desc: Low-lying, water-retentive fields with controlled inlet/outlet.
Strong bunds, trenches/refuge pond, screened flow points and harvest channel.
Carp or locally suited species matched to water depth, salinity and crop calendar.
Avoid harmful pesticides; shift to natural/safer pest management.
Regular visits by agriculture + fisheries teams during first crop cycle.
Farmer groups, aggregators, fish markets and cold chain for better returns.

blocks.label: Officer takeaway
blocks.text: pilots should be selected for technical feasibility first, then scaled through farmer confidence and demonstrated profitability.

sections.title: Relevance for paddy-growing districts of Andhra Pradesh
sections.source: Sources: AP Seeds; ANGRAU Paddy Outlook 2023–24; CGIAR 2023 note on IRFS in West Godavari.

blocks.title: Prioritise districts/mandals with:
items: Contiguous paddy area and assured water retention.
Existing canal or tank-based irrigation with manageable drainage.
Farmer interest in natural farming / lower chemical input practices.
Access to fish seed, local markets and fisheries extension.
Low-lying paddy patches where waterlogging is common.

items.desc: Krishna, East/West Godavari and adjoining delta mandals can test field-refuge models.
ANGRAU paddy outlook identifies West Godavari, Krishna, Srikakulam and Kakinada as major paddy-growing districts.
Integrated model can reduce chemical dependence and support biodiversity if field protocols are followed.
Freshwater fish availability improves household protein while rice yield is protected or improved.

blocks.text: Do not universalise. Start with feasibility screening and demonstration mandals before district-wide scale-up.

sections.title: District-level implementation model
sections.source: Sources: Implementation logic adapted from Assam and Qingtian cases; scheme convergence to be validated by state departments.

items.title: Feasibility mapping
items.body: Use paddy area, irrigation, water depth, drainage and pesticide-use pattern to shortlist mandals.

items.title: Demonstration clusters
items.body: Start with 5–10 fields per mandal through volunteer farmers, FPOs or natural farming groups.

items.title: Convergence
items.body: Pool agriculture, fisheries, RBK, MGNREGS, PMMSY/NFSM and local training resources.

items.title: Market planning
items.body: Tie up local fish vendors, ice boxes, collection points and rice branding before harvest.

sections.title: Monitoring framework and takeaways
sections.source: Key sources: Assam UNDP/NITI case; Arunachal Pradesh Fisheries note; FAO Qingtian GIAHS; Frontiers 2024; AP Seeds; ANGRAU Paddy Outlook; CGIAR.

items.desc: Paddy yield, fish yield, survival rate
Net income/acre vs paddy-only field
Fertilizer, pesticide and weeding labour
Retention days, depth, drainage events
Farmers trained, pilots completed, replication demand
Fish price, buyer linkage, aggregation volume

items.title: Start small, but design properly
items.body: Pilot only in technically suitable fields with water control and farmer consent.

items.title: Converge agriculture and fisheries teams
items.body: Joint field visits are essential during design, stocking and harvest.

items.title: Show income evidence
items.body: Compare with paddy-only plots; scale only when pilots show net returns and risk control.

blocks.label: Final message
blocks.text: rice–fish farming is a district productivity strategy, not just a farm technique.
